claims.reason: The passage states verbatim that Carnival is the largest global cruise company, among the largest leisure travel companies, and lists exactly those eight cruise lines.
Both revenue figures in the claim ($21.6B for FY ended 30 Nov 2023 and $27.6B for the twelve months to 31 Aug 2026) match exactly the metric values computed from the company's XBRL data.
Both EBITDA figures in the claim ($7.3 billion for FY ended 30 Nov 2025 and $7.3 billion for the twelve months to 31 Aug 2026) match the computed metric values exactly.
The passage states both that each brand meets a distinct set of consumer psychographics/vacation needs and that ship mobility enables moving vessels between regions to meet changing demand.
The passage directly states that no group of travel agencies under common control accounted for 10% or more of revenues in 2025.
The passage states overcapacity and competition in the cruise and land-based vacation industry may negatively impact cruise sales, pricing and destination options, matching the claim.
The metric values match the claim exactly.
The metric values show net leverage of 6.51x for FY ended 30 Nov 2023 and 3.10x for the twelve months to 31 Aug 2026, matching the claim of improvement.
The metric values show EBITDA/interest of 2.09x for FY ended 30 November 2023 and 6.21x for LTM to 31 August 2026, matching the claim's improvement.
The metric scorecard directly states FCF/debt was 3.3% in FY ended 30 Nov 2023 and 13.3% in the twelve months to 31 Aug 2026, matching the claim of improvement.

The metric values confirm total debt declined from $26.6B (FY ended 30 Nov 2025) to $23.9B (LTM to 31 Aug 2026), and the passage confirms issuance, modification, extinguishment, and refinancing transactions during the year.
Both claimed values match the computed metric values exactly.
Both stated figures match the computed XBRL metric values for the twelve months to 31 August 2026.
All three figures match the metric values exactly; dividends assumed zero because not reported.
Both figures are directly stated in the evidence.
The passage directly states the Revolving Facility may be borrowed or utilized through June 2030 subject to satisfaction of conditions.

The passage states the working capital deficit, its cause (customer deposits collected ahead of sailing), and that deposits are used with other cash sources to fund operations, service debt, and support capital investments.
All six maturity figures in the claim match the XBRL-computed metric values exactly.

claims.reason: The computed metric value from XBRL data shows near-term maturity cover of 2.66x for FY ending 30 November 2025, matching the claim.

The passage directly states the 2025 issuance of senior unsecured notes, borrowing under unsecured term loan facilities, and prepayment of notes due 2026 and 2027 and secured term loans due 2027 and 2028 using proceeds plus cash on hand.
The evidence directly states compliance with applicable covenants under debt agreements as of November 30, 2025.

The passage directly states that breaching covenants could trigger a default and that borrowings under other debt instruments with cross-default provisions may be accelerated or become payable on demand.
The passage supports overcapacity/competition reducing cruise sales and pricing, but the debt-service cash flow consequence is not stated in the evidence.
The risk factor passage directly states these factors could reduce cruise demand and negatively impact financial condition and operations.

The passage explicitly states future increases in global fuel prices would increase cruise ship operations costs and other expenses, and elsewhere that increased fuel costs lead to reduced profitability.
The passage directly states sustainability and emissions regulations may require capital investments in new equipment or technologies and payment for emission allowances, increasing costs.
All parts of the claim match the computed scorecard values exactly.
EBITDA / interest is band 3 with 25% weight (highest among factors, all others ≤20%), and near-term maturity cover is band 6 with 10% weight (lowest), matching the claim.
All four factors match the scorecard: Debt/EBITDA band 4 at 20%, net leverage band 4 at 10%, FCF/debt band 4 at 20%, and liquidity coverage band 4 at 15%.
The passage confirms management 'surpassing the investment grade threshold,' and the SB grade is presented only as a computed internal scorecard from XBRL metrics, not a credit rating.

Evidence states Carnival is the largest global cruise company with a portfolio of cruise lines, no travel-agency group ≥10% of revenues, and lists overcapacity/competition, geopolitical uncertainty, higher fuel costs, and emissions-related costs as risks.
